CFG-1.title: Implement Configuration Management APIs (Create, Read, Update, Delete) for Track Configurations
CFG-1.description:
Type: Story. Component: Backend / Configuration Module. Implement REST controller handlers that let an authenticated user manage their own track configurations. A configuration links a user to a track (TrackImage) and holds a name, a direction and optional polygons; it can also have associated geofences (GeoFence). Every operation is scoped to the logged-in user (req.user.id).
Files: a configuration controller exporting addNewConfiguration, getAllConfigurations, getSingleConfiguration, deleteConfiguration, updateConfiguration. Models: Configuration, TrackImage, GeoFence. Utilities: ApiResponse, ApiError, http-status-codes.
Functional requirements:
1. Add: body trackId, configurationName, direction (required), polygons (optional); 400 'All Fields are required' if a required field is missing; create with userId = req.user.id; 200 { status: 'Config Added successfully' }.
2. Get all: the user's configurations, each including track and geoFences; 404 'Configuration Not Found' if none; 200 with the list.
3. Get single: configurationId URL param; match configurationId AND userId, include track; 404 if no match, else 200.
4. Update: configurationId URL param; body configurationName, polygons, direction; only for the owner; 404 if no rows updated, else 200.
5. Delete: configurationId URL param; only for the owner; 404 if nothing deleted, else 200.
Non-functional: every handler uses try/catch and forwards errors with next(error); responses use ApiResponse.result, errors use ApiError with standard HTTP status codes; every query is filtered by userId; endpoints sit behind the auth middleware.
acceptance_criteria: POST create returns 200 and persists the configuration with the correct userId when all required fields are provided.
POST create returns 400 when trackId, configurationName or direction is missing.
GET all returns only the authenticated user's configurations, with track and geoFences included.
GET all returns 404 when the user has no configurations.
GET single returns the configuration with its track for the owner, and 404 for a non-existent ID or another user's configuration.
PUT/PATCH update modifies configurationName, polygons and direction for the owner, and returns 404 otherwise.
DELETE removes the configuration for the owner, and returns 404 otherwise.
A user cannot read, update or delete another user's configuration.
Unhandled errors are passed to the error-handling middleware.
